units.translation: ⟦1⟧ is a kind of dative of disadvantage, and it is not necessary, with Heimsoeth, to make ⟦2⟧ out of ⟦3⟧; for thus, or rather: thus is the following ⟦4⟧. Elaboration of what is contained in ⟦5⟧ or ⟦6⟧.

783 ⟦1⟧ also [Cho.] 281, there however of human disease; the length of the first syllable (manuscripts in both places with 1) is guaranteed by Martial XI, 98, 5. With Paley's proposed transposition ⟦2⟧ (see above) I cannot agree, since the two adjectives with a- are better kept together: ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧⟦6⟧ ⟦7⟧⟦8⟧, above 385 ⟦9⟧, 564 ⟦10⟧, etc., although one could compare ⟦11⟧ ⟦12⟧ for the other order. ⟦13⟧, ⟦14⟧, ⟦15⟧. Cf. 511 ⟦16⟧ Pauw for ⟦17⟧ Δ. Μ; ⟦18⟧ is in any case to be written as there.

⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧ can be referred to the lichen itself, which has neither leaves nor fruits; better, however, to understand them of the effect on plants and trees. ⟦3⟧ of fruit is certainly unusual, but no more so than ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧; in any case, leaves and children are an impossible combination, and at least the fruits must be thought of as well. At line 803 the threat uttered here is referred only to the seed.
in the birth-pangs of the bud
⟦1⟧ is ⟦2⟧ (schol.) as before ⟦3⟧; on ⟦4⟧ cf. ⟦5⟧ 1007, ⟦6⟧; alongside stands in Aeschylus ⟦7⟧. The 6 should be doubled, as well as in ⟦8⟧ 924; however, Euripides also has ⟦9⟧, Kühner-Blass II, 534.
⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧, where the arising of snakes and other harmful creatures is traced back to the staining of the earth with blood; from the ⟦3⟧ (801) naturally result diseases and destruction of men.
